one_line: API Evangelist third-party profile of HouseTrip (European vacation-rental marketplace, acquired by TripAdvisor 2016 and shut down): README boilerplate, apis.yml (2 KB), provenance.yml (6 KB), kin/ scoring stubs and screenshots; ~934 KB repo, no licence, created 2026-07-27, pushed 2026-09-12; zero listing, price or volume data.
abnb_use: None. Even as competitor-landscape colour (gap #9) it only records that a defunct platform once published an API; there is no endpoint to call and no historical supply/price series behind it.
reasoning: gh api confirms 934 KB of YAML metadata, screenshots and a scoring stub with no data directory, and the README states outright that the repository contains no software and is an independent profile of a public API surface. HouseTrip itself has been dead since the 2016 TripAdvisor acquisition, so nothing here is pullable. Dead/irrelevant by the run's own definition.

one_line: Single-file static dashboard (index.html, 50 KB, the whole repo) summarising Klook's supplier-side API capabilities — an embedded feature/capability matrix with an XLSX export button (SheetJS CDN), mentioning inventory, booking, price and JSON payload support; 0 stars, no licence, created and last pushed 2026-04-23.
abnb_use: At best a reference for what a tours-and-activities OTA exposes to its suppliers, i.e. background for Airbnb Experiences/Services competitive framing (gap #9). It carries no time series, no prices and no volumes, so it informs no KPI directly.
reasoning: Verified the repo holds exactly one 50 KB HTML file; grepping it shows only capability vocabulary (inventory, booking, price, JSON) inside a filterable matrix, not observations. No licence is declared, so reuse status is unclear. Worth one catalogue line as a Klook-adjacent artefact but not worth an agent pull.

one_line: Student Streamlit/LangChain chatbot (17 KB repo, 1 star, last push 2024-08-18, no licence) whose reusable part is ScrapeGetYourGuide.py (7 KB, Selenium/Chrome + BeautifulSoup) pulling activity-page fields (highlights, description) from GetYourGuide, plus ScrapeGoogle.py for link discovery; no data committed.
abnb_use: Only as a worked example of how to lift tour/activity page fields from a GetYourGuide listing — an Airbnb Experiences comparator (gap #9). It selects highlight text rather than price or availability, so even run it would not yield a pricing or volume panel.
reasoning: Read the actual scraper: it is Selenium driving a real browser against getyourguide.com CSS selectors from Aug 2024, so it is both a third-party-site scraper (a terms-of-service decision for a human, per the run rules) and almost certainly stale. Nothing is persisted in the repo, and the app also needs an OpenAI key. Catalogue as method, leave unrun.

one_line: Official ExpediaGroup Rapid (EPS) Java/Kotlin SDK, Apache-2.0, 6 stars, last push 2025-12-22, ~55 MB repo whose substantive artefact is specs.yaml (1.16 MB OpenAPI description of the Rapid lodging API: property content, shop/availability, rates, booking) plus generated code/, docs/ and examples/; the API itself needs an Expedia Partner Solutions key.
abnb_use: Documents, from Expedia's own org, the exact field surface of the feed carrying Brand Expedia/Hotels.com/Vrbo lodging supply and rates — the authoritative schema for a competitor supply/ADR panel (gap #9) and a useful reference for what a realised-rate feed would even contain (gap #2). Useless without partner credentials.
reasoning: Confirmed via gh api that specs.yaml (1,161,203 bytes) is committed and the licence is Apache-2.0, so the spec is freely readable; but Rapid is gated behind an Expedia Partner Solutions contract and API key, which the run rules put squarely in catalog_only. The SDK is a client, not data — pulling it would yield schema text and zero observations.

one_line: MIT-licensed MCP server (157 KB, 5 stars, last push 2025-09-16) wrapping Channex.io's channel-manager API — CRUD over properties, room_types and rate_plans, i.e. the ARI objects a property manager pushes to Airbnb, Booking.com and Vrbo; .env.example shows it requires the operator's own CHANNEX API key, and the repo ships no data.
abnb_use: Shows the schema a cross-OTA rate/inventory comparison panel would need (host-side ADR and availability across Airbnb vs Vrbo vs Booking, gap #9) and is a live pointer to how PMS-side data is structured. It cannot produce observations for us because it only reads listings the credential-holder controls.
reasoning: Directory listing confirms .env.example, Dockerfile, docs/ and a DISCLAIMER.md but no data files; the homepage points at Channex's API docs, which are account-gated. Because it touches Airbnb listings via a channel manager and needs credentials we do not have, it is catalog_only on two separate grounds. Licence (MIT) is fine; the blocker is access.
